notes.title: Patch Preview - New Content, Optimizations, Telekinesis Changes & More
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/81cd8849e0be01194fecb543cf3d85039ccb59ef.gif[/img]

Greetings, Wizards! We'll be releasing a large update tomorrow to inject some new creatures into the game while also improving stability and addressing some gameplay and balance issues. Your support and feedback has played a direct role in helping to identify bugs and balance issues, and we want to thank you greatly for sharing your feedback with us here on Steam, on [url=twitter.com/playcitadel]Twitter[/url] and through our support email!

[b](Scroll down to read about bug fixes and balance changes)[/b]

[h1]New Game Content[/h1]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/04fb664504da3eef9712e4c6b243a7e5a134d1f9.jpg[/img]
[b][u]Infernal Dragon[/u][/b]
The Infernal Dragon is a towering nightmare of jagged fangs, spiraling horns and dense, rippling muscle. Most scholars agree that the Infernal Dragon was once similar in size and appearance to the common dragons of Ignus, but after longterm exposure to demonic energy it has become a twisted abomination that exists only to terrorize those who would venture too far into the untamed Tundra of the north.

Approach the Infernal Dragon with extreme caution. If you are compelled to engage in combat with this formidable adversary be sure to bring allies and a healthy supply of rejuvenate provisions.  It will be a long, hard fight, but in the end you will be rewarded handsomely with significant experience and a bounty of rare and valuable crafting resources.

Some say it’s possible to tame and ride such creatures, but most regard this is as wild speculation by mad men and fools…


[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/114766d7a08cf33134a5d9c990456378d1b47e7b.png[/img]
[b][u]Skeleton Warriors[/u][/b]
The same evil magic that delivered the scourge of Imps and Demons unto this world has been used to reanimate the ancient dead of Ignus’ ancient warring houses. These Skeleton Warriors, who have risen from millennia of slumber, are fast and swift attackers who aim to catch their opponents off guard and attack by clawing and biting. Skeletons tend to coalesce in groups, and can easily surround you if you let them get too close. Fighting from a distance is recommended.


[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/ca206324ad686b421c7347e052dbad235f0ed1cc.png[/img]
[b][u]Wild Boar[/u][/b]
Though it may appear to be nothing more than a simple beast of burden, the Wild Boar is actually quite dangerous when encountered in its natural habitat. They are aggressive, impulsive beasts that have often been observed lashing out at perceived threats. A minor threat for seasoned mages, but newly minted wizards should be wary in their presence.


[h1]Fixes, Optimizations and Balance Changes[/h1]

[b][u]Optimizations[/u][/b]
We’ve made an important change in the backend of the game that should make performance and stability on populated servers up to ten times better. The source of a lot of our server issues stems from a bug in the Unreal Engine itself: while UE’s distance culling system does not draw objects within a certain distance of the player, it was still sorting the priority of tens of thousands of undrawn objects every single frame. 

We’ve created our own custom distance culler to combat this, which will exclude objects at an extreme distance from the prioritization process.  This should greatly improve performance and reduce structure download times. 

[b][u]Telekinesis[/u][/b]
After listening to your feedback and commentary it has become obvious to us that our current implementation of Telekinesis needed a little rethinking. We wanted to ensure it would not become a tool for griefing, but clearly that did not end up being the case. To those that lost their hard work to the spell, we do sincerely apologize.

We didn’t want to just turn off structure Telekinesis, so we came up with the following solution: along with now never working on PVE structures (as it should never have), Telekinesis will no longer be usable on any structure that has been claimed by a throne. If you want to throw structure pieces now it can only happen with structures that have been rendered abandoned. This means that another player can no longer use the spell to casually dismantle your fortress. As with all balance changes, we will be monitoring this closely to see how it plays with the current layout of the game.

[b][u]Spell Improvements[/u][/b]
We’ve tidied up a number of issues related to spell cooldowns, key among them being the weapon swapping exploit. After tomorrow’s patch you will no longer be able to rapdily swap weapons with ‘G’ to cancel cooldowns and spam high level, high cooldown spells. Some players took advantage of this bug to gain a significant advantage in PVP fights, and we wanted to ensure it was patched up to prevent griefing.

Additionally, we’ve added ranges to many of the game’s spells. Spells like Fireball previously had unlimited range which was problematic from the perspective of both PVP balance and server performance. Enemies could spam Fireballs from miles away and it would be impossible for the recipient to retaliate, and Fireballs shot into the air would continue to exist and travel indefinitely, straining the server after long periods of time. These two issues should now no longer exist with Wednesday’s patch.

[b][u]Decay Modifiers for Private Servers[/u][/b]
Your server, your rules. We implemented the new decay system to reduce strain on our official servers, but we want to ensure that private server owners have the flexibility to opt out. After Wednesday’s update you will have the ability to either decrease/increase the decay rate or turn it off altogether. 

[b][u]Much More[/u][/b]
There will be a ton of other tweaks, fixes and improvements in the patch: Camera sensitivity options, pet inventory fixes and much more.  Stay tuned for the details and full changelog tomorrow. We greatly appreciate your patience as we patch up the game and make it a more stable and balanced experience!


[h1]Update Livestream[/h1]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/3753924e6343aeba616e63b04272c332c6894a1c.png[/img]

We're doing it live! Join us tomorrow at 4pm EDT to see us walkthrough the new content and fixes, and listen to us talk about the future of Citadel. Hop over to twitch.tv/playcitadel and give us a follow to make sure you don't miss out!

- Blue Isle Studios

tags.bug: The source of a lot of our server issues stems from a bug in the Unreal Engine itself: while UE’s distance culling system does not draw objects within a certain distance of the player, it was still sorting the priority of tens of thousands of undrawn objects every single frame.

tags.balance_change: Telekinesis will no longer be usable on any structure that has been claimed by a throne. If you want to throw structure pieces now it can only happen with structures that have been rendered abandoned. This means that another player can no longer use the spell to casually dismantle your fortress.

tags.bug: After tomorrow’s patch you will no longer be able to rapdily swap weapons with ‘G’ to cancel cooldowns and spam high level, high cooldown spells. Some players took advantage of this bug to gain a significant advantage in PVP fights, and we wanted to ensure it was patched up to prevent griefing.

tags.balance_change: Spells like Fireball previously had unlimited range which was problematic from the perspective of both PVP balance and server performance. Enemies could spam Fireballs from miles away and it would be impossible for the recipient to retaliate, and Fireballs shot into the air would continue to exist and travel indefinitely, straining the server after long periods of time.

tags.feature: After Wednesday’s update you will have the ability to either decrease/increase the decay rate or turn it off altogether.
Camera sensitivity options, pet inventory fixes and much more.

notes.title: Patch Notes - 7/30/2017
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/d1cd7a56a5ad50d11cc995436eaa809df4079e3e.jpg[/img]

Good afternoon! We’re deploying another patch today to apply a small change to our structure degradation system. Lag and connectivity issues increase as junk structures gather on a server; to prevent this, we’re putting a system in place to remove abandoned thrones and clean up old structures with no ownership attached to them. This change will work as a means of improving longterm server performance and stability.

[b]The following will take effect after the game and our servers have been updated:[/b]

- Thrones will decay in 10 days unless you replace them or heal them
- If abandoned (dethroned), wood pieces will decay in roughly 5 hours
- If abandoned (dethroned), stone pieces will decay in roughly 10 hours
- If abandoned (dethroned), ornate pieces will decay in roughly 24 hours
- If abandoned (dethroned), magic and decorative structures will decay in roughly 5 hours

We’ve also made a few behind the scenes changes to help people attempting to join populated official servers. Please ensure your client is up-to-date, and allow time for the update to roll out to servers.

We apologize for the gameplay disruption, and appreciate your support as we work to improve stability and performance.

-	Blue Isle Studios

notes.title: Content Update & Patch Notes - 7/28/2017
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/bceb2233264a5b1e77d6cdb2e7d46ea24bd7aaa4.gif[/img]

It’s full steam ahead for us here at Blue Isle Studios! We’ve been absolutely blown away by the warm reception we’ve received since our Early Access launch two days ago, and have been working tirelessly to crush bugs, tweak gameplay balance and prepare new and awesome content for you guys to enjoy.

[b](Scroll down for full patch notes including bug and exploit fixes. Give a moment once the patch has been rolled out via Steam for the servers to update to the new version.)[/b]

[h1]Content Drop: Iron Armor & Bear Claw Gauntlet[/h1]
We’re ready to put out our first content update, which adds five new crafting recipes for the early levels of the game. Since we know most of you are still finding your footing in Ignus, we figured you’d appreciate a few more early-game options to add a little variety to your experience. Here’s what we’ve got for you:

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/1fd65b9681b146673f2cf743c65481f7450208f5.jpg[/img]

First up is the newest addition to our lineup of armor types: Iron Armor. Once you’ve unlocked the Iron set in the Knowledge Tree you’ll be able to repurpose the natural iron deposits of Ignus into an extremely robust protective garb. Just don’t skimp on the Carrying Capacity! The dense, metal plating that covers this substantial set of armor is extremely heavy, and can be cumbersome for mages who aren’t ready for the additional burden. 

This set is perfect for players adopting a close-range tank-style playstyle, but less ideal for mages interested in long-range, nimble combat. Despite being a low-tier set, the iron armor is pretty demanding from a crafting perspective. You’ll have to gather a heck of a lot of Iron Ingots, Rune Crystal, Leather and Cloth if you’ll want the whole set.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/f880c3f72a23bc0d971d8b27cad63097e542bbd7.jpg[/img]

For those interested in a more barbaric vibe, we’ve also added the brand new Bear Claw Gauntlet. Hunt and kill the savage Bears of Ignus and use their Pelts and Bones to create this intimidating new weapon. Though it may look primitive, the Bear Claw Gauntlet is a great early-game choice for casting the devastating damage-over-time spells the gauntlet sub-category is known for.

[h1]Patch Notes[/h1]
We’ve also made a bunch of changes, including bug and exploit fixes and balance adjustments.

The biggest change you’ll notice is that we’ve buffed structures by [b]a lot[/b]. We’ve been hearing your feedback that the current means of raiding is just too aggressive. We’re implementing this buff as a temporary measure to mitigate the potential for griefing while we work on a more elegant solution in the future. (Note: Existing structures will unfortunately not have their HP update, but new ones will have the effect applied. We’ll deploy a free refill on all structure HP with our next patch).

We’ve also cleaned up a few key exploits. Swapping potions no longer gives you their effect for free, and we’ve also made it so that you can’t kill a high level friend at a low level to get insane amounts of XP. Additionally, we've removed an exploit that allowed some players to have zero HP and become unkillable.

Lastly, thanks to the out-pouring of bug reports and crash logs you’ve sent us, we’ve managed to inject another round of crash fixes and server optimizations into the game. 

Here’s the full change list:
[list]
[*]Various crash fixes
[*]Various server optimizations
[*]Bear Claw Gauntlet added to the game
[*]Iron Armor added to the game
[*]/ban command now properly works for server admins
[*]Swapping potions no longer gives their effect for free
[*]PVP XP rebalanced to avoid exploitation
[*]Structure HP increased[/list]

(Note: You may find yourself unable to use Extract on small beach stones and medium Rune Crystal deposits after this patch. This is a known issue and will be fixed in the next update.)

notes.title: Citadel Weekly Review 7/28/2017
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/15ce3cd96120eccbb1dca2dc18af094cf526c5af.png[/img]

[i]Welcome to the Weekly Review! Every Friday we’ll break down the latest happenings in the world of Citadel: Forged with Fire. Check back weekly for info on game updates, events, community content, contests and much more![/i]

[h1]Launch Day![/h1]
On Wednesday, July 26th, Citadel: Forged with Fire was finally unleashed upon the world! We’ve been extremely pleased with the overall reception of the game, and have been absorbing your feedback and bug reports to improve the game as we continue to work through the early days of Early Access. We know that there’s still a lot of work to done, and we’re working long hours here to support the game.

We’ve said it before, and we’ll say it again now: Thank you for your support, input and overall enthusiasm for Citadel: Forged with Fire! We know you have high hopes for the future of the game, and we want to promise you that we’re committed to heavily supporting the game in both the short and longterm. We’ll be sharing an Early Access roadmap with you very soon that will detail the next 8-12 months of our development, so stay tuned!

[h1]First Patches[/h1]
Though launch was definitely a moment to celebrate, we understand that this is but the beginning of our Early Access journey. We’ve been working like fiends, preparing fixes for bugs and tweaking balance. Check out our patch notes from the week (and expect another patch later today):

[b]Patch Notes 7/27/2017 -  [/b]http://steamcommunity.com/games/487120/announcements/detail/1438189897662165578

[b]Patch Notes 7/26/2017 - [/b]http://steamcommunity.com/games/487120/announcements/detail/1438189897658673920


[h1]First Content Drop[/h1]
While our programmers have been chipping away at bugs, our artists have been hard at work preparing our first content drop. Our first such update adds five new crafting recipes for the early levels of the game. Since we know most of you are still finding your footing in Ignus, we figured you’d appreciate a few more early-game options to add a little variety to your experience. Here’s what you can expect from our update later today:

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/1fd65b9681b146673f2cf743c65481f7450208f5.jpg[/img]
First up is the newest addition to our lineup of armor types: [b]Iron Armor[/b]. This set offers fantastic damage resistance at the expense of extreme weight and a difficult set of crafting recipes. Perfect for players adopting a close-range tank-style playstyle.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/f880c3f72a23bc0d971d8b27cad63097e542bbd7.jpg[/img]
For those interested in a more barbaric vibe, we’ve also added the brand new [b]Bear Claw Gauntlet[/b]. Hunt and kill the savage Bears of Ignus and use their Pelts and Bones to create this intimidating new weapon.

[h1]Fantastic Castle Build Contest[/h1]
We had a community castle building contest earlier this week, and some of the submissions were amazing! Congratulations to our top 5 winners, who won a full copy of the game!

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/3ae2ea5ada02ac9b19d005e5d0e05e838bb16ee2.png[/img]
[b]Stone Mage Tower - Zagwitz[/b]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/5ad5498d80a0f121401d42ef198cc6877b3f53af.png[/img]
[b]Wooden Dam – Crockodille[/b]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/fa77dadfc6f1b84bc554e7733061de7fb732a7d7.png[/img]
[b]Castle of the Eternal Darkness – Tilt Master[/b]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/4d966b613656b22a62596978bb9e527253fc697b.png[/img]
[b]Seaside Observatory – Neralyte[/b]

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KrPcuo2ysWI
[b]Stormwood Lagoon House - Vexx[/b]

[h1]Community Content[/h1]
The best part of launch, for us, has been watching the massive out-pouring of fantastic community content! We’ve had a blast watching all the streams and YouTube videos that have come out in the last few days. Here’s a selection of some of our favorites!

Ser Winter’s excitement at experiencing his first Broomstick flight had us all cracking up:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vQfQe7uhONg
PsiSyn was able to tame and ride a dragon with impressive speed!
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=D3X3kzkykA4
VERTiiGO GAMING’s strange encounter with a Pyrant Demon was particularly memorable:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sTKc5MAoowU
Roque Kazin made a terrific guide with 15 great tips for getting started in the game:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5IylQrGkJ-U

notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/84b6aff4c018d870583fd806cbda24c4b8d87a82.png[/img]

Good evening, denizens of Ignus! As part of our continued commitment to supporting and improving Citadel, we have prepared and deployed another patch to help alleviate some of the minor lingering issues you may have experienced since yesterday's launch. Today's patch brings with it the following changes:
[list]
[*]Various crash fixes and stability improvements
[*]Mouse inversion has now been added to our Settings menu
[*]VOIP optimizations and improvements allow for louder, clearer voice chat
[*]Fixed a bug causing all Respawn Stones to appear as respawn options on some servers. As part of this fix, Respawn Stones can now only be placed in structures with a Throne.
[*]Removed "Quit" from the death screen
[/list]
Thanks again for your support, and expect many more patches to come in the near future!

- Blue Isle Studios

notes.title: Patch Notes - 7/25/2017
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/f307a3d3683251a44251d6fe3a66b4dc58d3cf39.jpg[/img]

This is it! Tomorrow’s the big day! Citadel: Forged with Fire will be available for purchase on July 26th!

In addition to preparing a slew of fresh new servers to ensure we are prepared to meet launch demand, we’ve made some final little tweaks to the game’s balance to remove some critical exploits and solve some major bugs.

One of our biggest findings from the playtest was that structures were just too easy to raid. Walls could be smashed down with minimal effort, which cause some players a great deal of frustration. We’ve implemented changes to correct this problem.

We also received a lot of feedback suggesting that XP gained from spam building certain structure pieces was highly exploitable. It’s not ideal for anyone to have spam building of junk structures be an encouraged activity, so we’ve rebalanced a few things to make this a much less effective method of leveling.

Lastly, we made the choice, based on your feedback, to pull chest icons off the map entirely. You made it clear that finding these chests didn’t feel special, and we agree. Now you will be encouraged to explore the world to find these chests on your own, which should overall make the game feel more rewarding.

We’ve also made a few other key bug fixes and tweaks, so take a look at the expanded notes below. We hope to see you in-game very soon!

[h1]NPCs and Tames[/h1]
-	Dragons have had their damage and mana regen nerfed to ensure they are less OP in PVP
-	Tames no longer attack housemates, and can be safely parked at a shared House castle

[h1]Houses[/h1]
-	Respawn Stones now show up for players in the same House

[h1]Building[/h1]
-	Structure pieces have had their health tripled
-	Thrones have been given an even greater buff (2.5k health -> 10k health)
-	XP gained from construction has been reduced
-	Single Scaffolding Piece: XP gain has been decreased and cost has been increased to prevent abuse
-	Fixed a bug that caused players to lose control of their home when moving their throne

 [h1]Other[/h1]
-	Chest icons have been removed from the map
-	Significant VOIP improvements
-	Display will now scale properly in 4:3 resolutions
-	Arrow keys can now be used for movement
-	FOV and other options can no longer be set ridiculously high or low by typing in the text field
-	Windows PC names no longer appear in House menu before a player creates a character
-	Server populations will display properly in the server browser
-	Server and performance optimizations

notes.title: Feature Highlight: Flight
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/036e0417ff5586588baebccc082983a9df29405f.gif[/img]

[i]Welcome to today’s Feature Highlight! During the run-up to our Early Access launch on July 26th we’ll be taking a closer look at some of the fantastic features that make up Citadel: Forged with Fire. Keep checking back for more in-depth gameplay reveals![/i]

[h1]Take To the Skies[/h1]
I pose to you a simple question: Why walk when you can fly?

An important thing for us in creating Citadel was ensuring that powerful, magically adept players feel powerful. We didn’t want the difference between level 2 and level 20 to be moderate damage increases on generic fireball spells; Growing in experience should feel significant, and flight is one of the many things we added to make sure this was the case.

There are three main ways you can achieve flight in Citadel: magical broomsticks, tamed airborne companions like dragons and giant eagles, or potent flight elixirs. Each method has its pros and cons, and will be more accessible to different players depending on the path you take as you level up.

[h1]You See This? This… Is My Broomstick![/h1]
One of the most accessible means of flight is the broomstick. Though you will have to reach a certain level to custom-craft your own, it is not uncommon to loot one while adventuring in some of the more dangerous areas in the game.

Once equipped, broomsticks allow you to easily begin flying with the press of a button. Agile and highly maneuverable, broomsticks are the perfect mode of transportation for exploring or getting from point A to B. Just keep an eye on your mana; convenient though they may be, flying with a broomstick requires the use of your magical essence. You’ll want to stock lots of mana restoration items like herbs and potions if you’re planning on a lengthy trip.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/84b6aff4c018d870583fd806cbda24c4b8d87a82.png[/img]

[h1]Riding High[/h1]
Another much more difficult option for achieving flight is taming and mounting a winged creature. You’ll be able to unlock the Pacify spell once you’ve gained some considerable experience, but doing so is only half the battle. Not only will you have to find an opportunity to get close enough to an airborne beast to use the spell, but you’ll also have focus it on the monster for long enough for the effect to take hold. As you can imagine, Dragons are not keen to be tamed, so expect a struggle.

Despite being a lot of work to attain, winged mounts are a major step up from basic broomsticks. Let’s face it: riding a Dragon is a hundred times cooler. You will be able to fly without depleting your mana, and some winged mounts are even able to launch unique attacks.

[h1]Alchemy[/h1]
Finally, players who have used their experience and knowledge to research the appropriate alchemic recipe can craft flight granting potions. Once the required ingredients have been collected and the potion has been created, you can consume it to experience unrestricted flight without the aid of broom or beast. You are liberated to move freely in all directions without the burden of maintaining our mana pool or mounting and dismounting a large creature.

Of course, there’s always a downside. Like broomsticks, do draw from your pool of mana. If you’re 50 feet in the air when your mana runs dry, well, you know what to expect. Be mindful of this limitation and use flight potions in special situations rather than as a regular means of flight.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/a7c0765a4fbe560d9df34435cdac9c680566759b.gif[/img]

notes.title: Patch Notes - 7/19/2017
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/cb1940c00be6127304d44216b156649c7e5e3f7f.gif[/img]

Welcome to our very first Citadel: Forged with Fire patch notes post! We had an absolute blast watching all the streams and gameplay videos that came out during our first Closed Beta Test, and used all the feedback we observed to tweak the game’s balance and improve the gameplay experience for our next test. 

We noticed most players encountered issues with our NPC behavior. Enemies would give chase to players infinitely, and the only option to deal with them was to jump in a pool of water and snipe them from safety. To fix this, we’ve made a number of changes to our NPC AI, which should hopefully resolve this issue.

Spell balance was another thing we decided to take a look at coming out of last weekend. Players expected spells to be more powerful, so we went ahead and gave them some significant buffs. Additionally, we also addressed some audio and graphical issues that may have occurred (I’m looking at you Haste).

In addition to the above, we made some key changes to building and map presentation, and added a few small things here and there to make some confusing things a little more obvious. Oh, and we added VOIP!

Transparency and communication is a top priority for us as we move towards and beyond our Early Access launch, and we can’t wait to continue rapidly delivering new content, balance changes and bug fixes on a constant basis.

Take a look below, and we hope to see you in-game soon!



[h1]NPCs[/h1]
-	NPCs will now drop aggro when you run away. No more being chased from the Whispering Woods all the way up to Venturer’s Bane by 50 Orcs! 
-	NPC movement has been increased. You can run, and they’ll eventually lose interest, but don’t expect to be faster than a wolf while running backward now.
-	NPC perception has been decreased. Orcs will no longer spot you from a mile away, so you will now be able to better avoid unwanted encounters.
-	Forest Guardian rock  throws should now work properly instead of harmlessly exploding near you.
-	NPC health has been balanced. We’ve made it so early game enemies (near starter towns) are a little easier and late game enemies (up north in the Tundra regions) are less abusable.

[h1]Structures[/h1]
-	Doors and door frames have been renamed to avoid confusion. You do not have to build a door frame to build a door. They are two independent building options.
-	Doors should no longer render off the hinges and should be placed properly within the wall. As you’d expect from a door.
-	All references to “Nexus” replaced with “Throne” for clarity.
-	Some adjustments to build menu icons to make things a little easier to understand.

[h1] Spells/Combat[/h1]
-	Lots of spell buffs. Players last weekend observed that spells were not doing as much damage as basic melee, which felt a little off. Damage, cooldowns and mana costs have all been adjusted to give them a little more oomf.
-	You can no longer fire spells off while swimming. Now water will be useful in escaping mobs, but cannot be used to cheese enemies. 
-	Telekinesis is now very expensive and a lot weaker. We want this spell to be underpowered at launch, and we’ll slowly readjust and increase its power as we go. We don’t want this spell to become too overpowered and have it ruin anyone’s experience.
-	Pacify has been rebalanced. You can now only tame creatures ten levels higher than you or less.
-	Extract costs less mana to cast to make resource gathering less tedious.

[h1]Other[/h1]
-	VOIP is now live! Push “-“ in-game and start getting chatty!
-	Mana and health pools regenerate your vitals a lot slower to avoid abuse. Our plan for mana and health pools was to have them as a places where you can rest for a moment and top up your vitals. This is more in-line with that objective.
-	Saddles are now craftable to allow creature riding.
-	The House window will now display properly for all players.
-	Empty chests now properly show as opened.
-	Haste, Bloodlust and Blue Aura VFX now stop when the buff wears off.
-	Resource rich rocks are now glowier and more noticeable.
-	Lots of map presentation tweaks.

- Resource rich rocks are now glowier and more noticeable.

tags.feature: - VOIP is now live! Push “-“ in-game and start getting chatty!
- Saddles are now craftable to allow creature riding.

tags.balance_change: - NPCs will now drop aggro when you run away. No more being chased from the Whispering Woods all the way up to Venturer’s Bane by 50 Orcs!
- NPC movement has been increased. You can run, and they’ll eventually lose interest, but don’t expect to be faster than a wolf while running backward now.
- NPC perception has been decreased. Orcs will no longer spot you from a mile away, so you will now be able to better avoid unwanted encounters.
- NPC health has been balanced. We’ve made it so early game enemies (near starter towns) are a little easier and late game enemies (up north in the Tundra regions) are less abusable.
- Doors and door frames have been renamed to avoid confusion. You do not have to build a door frame to build a door. They are two independent building options.
- All references to “Nexus” replaced with “Throne” for clarity.
- Some adjustments to build menu icons to make things a little easier to understand.

- Lots of spell buffs. Players last weekend observed that spells were not doing as much damage as basic melee, which felt a little off. Damage, cooldowns and mana costs have all been adjusted to give them a little more oomf.
- You can no longer fire spells off while swimming. Now water will be useful in escaping mobs, but cannot be used to cheese enemies.

- Telekinesis is now very expensive and a lot weaker. We want this spell to be underpowered at launch, and we’ll slowly readjust and increase its power as we go. We don’t want this spell to become too overpowered and have it ruin anyone’s experience.
- Pacify has been rebalanced. You can now only tame creatures ten levels higher than you or less.
- Extract costs less mana to cast to make resource gathering less tedious.

- Mana and health pools regenerate your vitals a lot slower to avoid abuse. Our plan for mana and health pools was to have them as a places where you can rest for a moment and top up your vitals. This is more in-line with that objective.

notes.title: Feature Highlight: Creature Taming & Riding
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/acf8a6b834484112eb2de6ef36ec9ff321404cbe.gif[/img]

[i]Welcome to today’s Feature Highlight! During the run-up to our Early Access launch on July 26th we’ll be taking a closer look at some of the fantastic features that make up Citadel: Forged with Fire. Keep checking back for more in-depth gameplay reveals![/i]

[h1]Creature Feature[/h1]
What good is having a selection of incredible magic spells like Conflagration, which lets you bring meteors down from the heavens, if there’s nothing to use them on? 

Fortunately, that’s not a dilemma you’ll have to confront with Citadel. As beautiful as the world is, it’s also littered with a wide variety of dangerous monsters and beasts just aching for a fight. Oblige them!

Ravenous Bears and Direwolves pose an early challenge, but as you grow in power and travel further into the wilds you’ll encounter creatures that present a significantly greater threat. Territorial Dragons patrol the rugged terrain of the tundra, Orcs travel the plains in packs looking for something to kill, and Giant Demons lay in wait for wandering adventurers unwise enough to enter their domain. Hunt them down to grow in experience and acquire rare resources and loot. 

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/2504c1bbade850c483627a48b33f6506da815ed8.png[/img]

[h1]Beast Friends Forever[/h1]
Dealing with the creatures of Citadel isn’t just a kill-or-be-killed situation; there is another option. Once you’ve grown strong enough you will eventually unlock access to the Pacify spell, which you can use to tame your enemies and have them aid you in battle. Wounded enemies are much less resistant to taming magic, so be prepared for a battle if you want to earn the loyalty of high-level beasts!

The best part? This effect can be maintained [i]indefinitely[/i]. Any monsters you tame become your companion, and will do as you command so long as you maintain their loyalty with craftable Soul Binding Scrolls. Bring them with you to watch your back on your adventures, or have them hold position and guard your home against raiders. Just like you, they will level up and grow in strength as they triumph in combat.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/e9c7aeb4393e256bdfb90ebc69200392c88fb96e.jpg[/img]

[h1]Ride Together, Fly Together[/h1]
But wait, there’s more! Some creatures can even be fit with a riding saddle once they’ve been tamed, giving you the ability to use them as a mount. Ride land-based creatures like Bears, Horses or Direwolves to cover large stretches of terrain with ease and comfort. 

You can even take to the skies with the help of winged beasts. Giant Eagles and Dragons, elusive and evasive as they may be, can actually be mounted once tamed. Yes, that’s correct; you can ride Dragons.

Additionally, many creatures have the ability to launch unique attacks once you’ve hopped on their backs, making them also valuable in situations where you need a little more offensive power. Raiding an opposing House’s fortress? Perhaps it would be strategically wise to use a Dragon’s fire breath to provide air support for your allies on the ground.

notes.title: Feature Highlight: Building
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/791fdc64cf90159ae7fa9e42cde4f8ae94221e05.gif[/img]

[i]Welcome to today’s Feature Highlight! During the run-up to our Early Access launch on July 26th we’ll be taking a closer look at some of the fantastic features that make up Citadel: Forged with Fire. Keep checking back for more in-depth gameplay reveals![/i]

[h1]Build Your Empire[/h1]
Wizard Fact: You’re not a proper wizard if you don’t live in a cool tower, castle or dungeon!

When we decided we wanted to include structure building in our game, we made it a top priority to ensure we did it right. Our vision is to have a building system that is as easy to use as it is flexible and open-ended – we don’t want our wizards to feel stuck building the same cookie-cutter castles.

We’re confident that we’ve struck this balance: Citadel has literally hundreds of construction pieces to unlock and use. Build anywhere with complete, unrestricted freedom. Simply gather the resources you need – via conventional scavenging or with the aid of speedy resource extraction spells – find a spot worthy of your masterpiece, and get to work!

As you level up your character you will unlock the ability to fortify your creations with stronger resources and craft more elaborate decorative and functional items like thrones, storage chests and crafting stations.

[h1]Houses[/h1]
Although you’re free to build a modest home on your own, if you want to create something truly impressive you’ll have to work with other players. The best way to do this is to form a House. Players within a House share their Thrones with each other, and are therefore better enabled to share resources and build large-scale structures. Gather your friends, form a House, and create a massive kingdom!

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/07a543734953e3ad7dc236b1c1b663b68eea5925.gif[/img]

[h1]Magic Structures: Enchanted Amenities[/h1]
A wizard would also not be content with hanging their pointed hat in a mere shell of stone and wood. As you know, magic extends to everything in Citadel, and that includes the buildings you’ll be creating. Using your growing magical prowess, you will be able to construct an array of magically imbued structures including defensive shields, attack towers, mana pools, respawn stones and many more. Use these structures to buff yourself and protect your property from foes.


[h1]Endless Possibilities[/h1]
We’ve created the tools so you can express your creativity and make your own unique mark on Citadel’s sprawling landscape. We here at Blue Isle Studios have had a ton of fun building absurd and elaborate castles, and we can’t wait to see what you guys cook up once you get your hands on the game! In the meantime, check out these examples of what we’ve come up with:

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/9726022b652c988d0f1b02be2d223192d33471cc.jpg[/img]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/19adb67afe42f695c931ea6360b89ad87c53badb.jpg[/img]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/ea56d920070fac3d478e02df0b208197d9bcb47f.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Feature Highlight: Magic
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/1e864f3d2c82c7f5448500e3c1b84e46df85a4e7.gif[/img]

[i]Welcome to today’s Feature Highlight! During the run-up to our Early Access launch on July 26th we’ll be taking a closer look at some of the fantastic features that make up Citadel: Forged with Fire. Keep checking back for more in-depth gameplay reveals![/i]


[h1]Master the Arcane Arts[/h1]
Today we begin our series of Feature Highlights by taking a look at the force at the center of just about everything in Ignus: Magic! As you explore, fight monsters, and build the castle of your dreams you will also grow in experience. You’ll want to use this experience to expand your knowledge of the arcane arts if you’ll have any hope of thriving in this harsh world.

At launch, Citadel will offer you a diverse range of powerful spells, with many more to come in the future. You can do some really cool stuff with our magic system: not just combat, but also beast taming, telekinesis, resource collection and much more.

[b]Pacify:[/b] This spell gives you the power to charm enemies and use them as combat allies; Some enemies can even be used as mounts! We’ll talk about this spell in more detail in a future Feature Highlight, so stay tuned.

[b]Extract:[/b] We decided a high level wizard would have too much dignity to be caught hunched over gathering sticks and stones, so we came up with the Extract spell. Using this power, mages can effortlessly suck materials out of giant rocks, trees and other objects to accumulate large quantities of building resources with ease. Build massive castles and fortresses without the crushing tedium of resource gathering.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/39bf9a3a457beae71403fe5e7d204e5d0ee53278.gif[/img]

[b]Telekinesis:[/b] As your grasp over the magical arts grows you will eventually unlock the ability to levitate physical objects and propel them at high speeds. While you may be thinking you’ve seen this type of thing in a hundred other games, we’ve taken it to a completely new level. Sure, you can use this spell to turn simple objects – rocks and branches, for example – into projectiles, but can you think of another game that lets you pick up and throw [i]entire freakin’ castles[/i]? Didn’t think so! 

I rest my case.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/11fb4a1d0b691ad6e76ae58475553ec097098db2.gif[/img]


[h1]Tools of the Trade[/h1]
You’ll also want to familiarize yourself with the four different types of tools used to harness these powers: Wands, Staves, Gauntlets and Melee Weapons. Some spells can only be performed with certain tools, so it’s important to take stock of what you’re wielding in certain situations; that beefy axe you found may cause devastating damage to enemies, but its limited range makes it incapable of providing long-range support.

[b]Wands:[/b] Wands are effective at espionage, quick movement and confusion. Wands are able to cast many precision ranged attacks, and often come with a cooldown reduction bonus making it perfect for those who like rapid-fire combat.

[b]Staves:[/b] Staves excel at ranged attacks and area-of-effect magic. Staff users are better suited in a support role rather than on the frontline. Many staves will offer a boost to a player’s maximum mana.

[b]Gauntlets:[/b] Gauntlets excel at beam type spells: they deliver high damage-over-time at the cost of significant mana drain. 

[b]Melee Weapons:[/b] Melee weapons like axes and swords excel at dealing huge amounts of damage, but at the cost of short range. They rely far less on magic, and therefore use less mana. 

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29650925/650dd29a284469045140d6b204554e01805c8e24.png[/img]

tags.feature: At launch, Citadel will offer you a diverse range of powerful spells, with many more to come in the future.
You can do some really cool stuff with our magic system: not just combat, but also beast taming, telekinesis, resource collection and much more.
This spell gives you the power to charm enemies and use them as combat allies; Some enemies can even be used as as mounts!
We decided a high level wizard would have too much dignity to be caught hunched over gathering sticks and stones, so we came up with the Extract spell.
Using this power, mages can effortlessly suck materials out of giant rocks, trees and other objects to accumulate large quantities of building resources with ease.
Build massive castles and fortresses without the crushing tedium of resource gathering.
As your grasp over the magical arts grows you will eventually unlock the ability to levitate physical objects and propel them at high speeds.

Sure, you can use this spell to turn simple objects – rocks and branches, for example – into projectiles, but can you think of another game that lets you pick up and throw [i]entire freakin’ castles[/i]?
You’ll also want to familiarize yourself with the four different types of tools used to harness these powers: Wands, Staves, Gauntlets and Melee Weapons.

Some spells can only be performed with certain tools, so it’s important to take stock of what you’re wielding in certain situations; that beefy axe you found may cause devastating damage to enemies, but its limited range makes it incapable of providing long-range support.
Wands are effective at espionage, quick movement and confusion.
Wands are able to cast many precision ranged attacks, and often come with a cooldown reduction bonus making it perfect for those who like rapid-fire combat.
Staves excel at ranged attacks and area-of-effect magic.
Staff users are better suited in a support role rather than on the frontline.
Many staves will offer a boost to a player’s maximum mana.
Gauntlets excel at beam type spells: they deliver high damage-over-time at the cost of significant mana drain.
Melee weapons like axes and swords excel at dealing huge amounts of damage, but at the cost of short range.
They rely far less on magic, and therefore use less mana.
